wp.copy_config_not_rewritable: The data copy was NOT performed. The source's wp-config.php does not hold its database settings as plain define('DB_NAME','…') statements (for example they come from getenv(), $_ENV, or another file via require), so the target's own database settings could not be written back after the copy and the target site would have connected to the SOURCE's database. The target site is untouched. Fix: convert the DB settings in the source's wp-config.php into plain define statements, or copy only the database (leave the Files box unchecked).
wp.copy_target_config_unreadable: The data copy was NOT performed. The database settings could not be read from the target site's own wp-config.php, and writing back a value we could not read would leave the target site unable to start. The target site is untouched.
wp.copy_config_not_merged: The data was copied. The source's wp-config.php settings could not be carried over; the target's own wp-config.php was restored from the backup, so the target still connects to its own database. Only the settings defined exclusively in the source's wp-config.php (WP_DEBUG, custom constants, salt keys) were not carried over.
wp.clone_config_not_rewritable: The clone was not created. The source's wp-config.php does not hold its database settings as plain define('DB_NAME','…') statements (for example they come from getenv(), $_ENV, or another file via require), so the new database settings could not be written into the clone and the clone would have connected to the SOURCE's (live) database. No site or database was created.
wp.clone_config_not_written: The clone was created but the new database settings could NOT be written into its wp-config.php: the clone may be connecting to the SOURCE's database — every change you make on what you believe is staging would alter live data. Fix wp-config.php by hand before using the clone.

panel.database.hardenHint: Sets a strong password if root has none (the panel stores it), removes anonymous and remote (root@'%') accounts, drops the empty default 'test' database, and TIGHTENS OVER-BROAD DATABASE GRANTS (so one customer's grant cannot cover another customer's database). root@localhost keeps working — panel access is not lost.
panel.database.hardenHintPg: PostgreSQL: removes the PUBLIC connect privilege that every database is created with — it let one customer's role connect to another customer's database and read its table and column names. Users with an explicit grant keep using their own database (schema public rights are granted too). Databases with NO explicit grantee are LEFT ALONE — revoking there would cut a working connection; they are listed separately in the report.

mail.autoresponder_script_failed: The auto-reply rule could not be written to the mail server.

panel.mail.listPostingPolicyOptions: anyone / subscribers (subscribers only) / allowed (listed addresses only)

panel.mail.listPolicyInvalid: Invalid policy. Allowed values: anyone, subscribers, allowed.

panel.mail.listAddAliasPrompt: Extra address to add to the list:

htaccess.deviation.access_before_rewrite: Access control (Deny/Require) runs BEFORE rewriting and against the original request path. Apache rewrites the URL first and then checks the target directory, so in Apache a rule that sends everything to index.php can disable a protection placed on /private/. AdaPanel is deliberately more protective here.
htaccess.deviation.directory_section: <Directory> sections are applied; Apache rejects them inside .htaccess.
htaccess.deviation.fatal_file_skipped: A .htaccess with a fatal syntax error is not applied, but the site does not return 500: the condition is reported in the panel and the request continues as if the file were absent.
htaccess.deviation.authuserfile_inside_r: AuthUserFile (htpasswd) must live UNDER the site root. Apache accepts any absolute path; on shared hosting that was the way to make the panel read its own files.
htaccess.deviation.directory_request_no_: For a directory request (/blog/) the file name is empty, so <Files>/<FilesMatch> sections do not match. Apache resolves the directory index (index.php) first and matches against that name.
htaccess.deviation.regex_timeout_stops_a: If a pattern times out, the ENTIRE evaluation stops, not just that rule. A half-applied rule set is more dangerous than one that was never applied.
htaccess.module_assembly_missing: The module assembly (AdaPanel.HtaccessModule) was not found in the server assembly cache (GAC), so the registration was NOT written. Pointing the registration at a missing assembly would fault every managed application on the server. Re-run the installer first.
htaccess.module_registered: The module was registered with IIS. The change takes effect once the application pools recycle.
htaccess.blocker.registration_unreadable: The IIS configuration could NOT be read, so whether the module is registered is unknown. Make sure the panel runs with administrative rights.
htaccess.blocker.module_not_registered: The module is NOT registered with IIS; .htaccess files are read but NOT applied to requests. Use the repair button below to register it.
htaccess.blocker.module_assembly_missing: The module assembly was not found on the server (GAC is empty). The installer needs to be re-run.
htaccess.blocker.module_type_mismatch: The module registered in IIS points at a DIFFERENT type; this registration does not belong to AdaPanel. The repair button fixes it.
htaccess.blocker.precondition_managed_ha: The module registration carries the "managedHandler" precondition: the module then runs only for managed requests and does NOT run for PHP or static file requests. Most of your .htaccess rules would not be applied. The repair button fixes the precondition.
htaccess.blocker.data_root_mismatch: The panel and the IIS module are looking at DIFFERENT data folders: the panel writes the switch file under its own data root, while the module uses the ADAPANEL_DATA_ROOT environment variable or the default %ProgramData%\AdaPanel folder. As a result the module can be loaded and running yet never see the rules you enabled. Either restore Panel:DataRoot to its default, or set ADAPANEL_DATA_ROOT on the server to match the panel data root and restart IIS.
